title: Yield and atom economy - 123 school
heading: Yield and atom economy
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. The formulas are in BINAS table 37H. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: What is a limiting reactant?

answers.c: the starting substance that is used up first
answers.d: the substance with the largest mass

questions.question: 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. You have 2.0 mol H<sub>2</sub> and 2.0 mol O<sub>2</sub>. Which substance is in excess?
Zn + 2 HCl → ZnCl<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>. You have 0.100 mol Zn and 0.50 mol HCl. How many moles of H<sub>2</sub> form?
N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> → 2 NH<sub>3</sub>. You have 1.0 mol N<sub>2</sub> and 6.0 mol H<sub>2</sub>. How many moles of NH<sub>3</sub> can form at most?
How do you calculate the yield (BINAS table 37H)?

answers.b: mass of product / mass of waste × 100%
answers.c: mass of desired product / mass of starting substances × 100%

questions.question: The theoretical yield is 25.0 g and you obtain 20.0 g. What is the yield?
The theoretical yield is 50 g and the yield is 70%. How many grams of product do you obtain?
Can the yield of a reaction be above 100% if you did everything correctly?
A student obtains a yield of 112%. What is a possible cause?

answers.b: the product was still wet or impure
answers.c: there was too little starting substance

questions.question: 4.86 g of Mg reacts with excess O<sub>2</sub> to give MgO. What is the theoretical yield of MgO? (M(MgO) = 40.30 g/mol)
You obtain 7.25 g of MgO and the theoretical yield is 8.06 g. What is the yield?
How do you calculate the atom economy (BINAS table 37H)?

answers.a: mass of waste / mass of desired product
answers.b: mass of desired product / mass of waste × 100%
answers.d: mass of desired product / total mass of starting substances × 100%

questions.question: What is the atom economy of an addition reaction with one product?
Calculate the atom economy for CaO in CaCO<sub>3</sub> → CaO + CO<sub>2</sub> (M: CaCO<sub>3</sub> 100.09, CaO 56.08 g/mol)
Calculate the atom economy for O<sub>2</sub> in 2 H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O + O<sub>2</sub> (M: H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> 34.02, O<sub>2</sub> 32.00 g/mol)
Calculate the atom economy for ethanol in C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> → 2 C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 2 CO<sub>2</sub> (M: glucose 180.16, ethanol 46.07 g/mol)
What is the E-factor (BINAS table 37H)?

answers.a: mass of waste / mass of starting substances × 100%
answers.c: mass of waste / mass of desired product
answers.d: mass of desired product / mass of waste

questions.question: In a process 5.0 kg of product and 20 kg of waste are formed. What is the E-factor?
Which E-factor belongs to the most environmentally friendly process?
From 40.0 g of starting materials 15.7 g of the desired product is formed; the rest is waste. What is the E-factor?
Which BINAS table contains the principles of green chemistry?
Which measure belongs to green chemistry?

answers.a: using a catalyst so that less energy is needed
answers.b: using an excess of a hazardous substance
answers.c: carrying out the reaction at the highest possible temperature
answers.d: using a solvent that is not reused

questions.question: What does a high atom economy mean for the environment?

answers.b: less waste per kg of product
answers.d: more waste per kg of product

questions.question: A reaction has an atom economy of 100%, but the yield is 60%. What does that mean?

answers.a: all atoms can end up in the product, but in practice some product is lost
answers.b: a lot of waste is formed because atoms are lost in the design
answers.d: the yield can never be lower than the atom economy

questions.question: In a factory starting materials continuously enter the reactor and product continuously leaves it. What is such a process called?
What is a substance in excess?

answers.a: a substance that is used up completely
answers.b: the substance with the smallest molar mass
answers.d: a starting substance of which some is left after the reaction
